subtitle: A one-number fix: the ISI IMP is address 22, not 86 as RFC 404 said.

tldr.problem: RFC 404 gave the wrong address for the IMP at ISI.
tldr.mechanism: This note says the address of the ISI IMP is 22 (decimal), not 86, and repeats the full corrected text.
tldr.outcome: All other numbers in RFC 404 were correct. The note updates RFC 404.

today: RFC 405 updates RFC 404 and has no recorded replacement. It is a historical record of an early ARPANET address change.

sections.title: The Correction
sections.content: This note corrects a typographic error in RFC 404. The address of the ISI IMP is 22 (decimal), not 86 as was erroneously stated. All other numbers in RFC 404 were correct.
sections.eli5: One number was typed wrong, so this note fixes it.

sections.title: The Corrected Text
sections.content:
The RAND IMP was temporarily removed from the network and a new IMP was installed at ISI. Some people and computers from RAND moved to ISI; in particular the RAND TENEX became the ISI TENEX.

The ISI IMP address is 22 (decimal) and the TENEX at ISI is Host number one, so the Network Address of the ISI TENEX is 86. The RAND IMP was to be re-installed early the next week, still as IMP number 7, and the IBM 360/65 at RAND would still have Network Address 7.
sections.eli5: A computer moved to a new building, so it got a new address. The old building keeps its address for when it reopens.

sections.title: What Changed and What Did Not
sections.content: Only one number changed: the IMP address 22 replaces the wrong 86. The Network Address of the ISI TENEX stays 86, because it is formed from IMP 22 and Host number one. The RAND numbers, 7 for the IMP and 7 for the IBM 360/65, are unchanged.
sections.eli5: Only the one wrong number was swapped; everything else stayed as first announced.
